thread.title: Is Under Armour slipping into irrelevance?

author: Tonya Garcia
title: Is Under Armour slipping into irrelevance?
text:
Bloomberg Analysts say Under Armour should beat fourth-quarter earnings expectations, but 2018 could be more challenging Heading into its fourth-quarter earnings report scheduled for Feb. 13, analysts are raising concerns about Under Armour Inc.’s relevance, with everything from the company’s products to its choice of a flagship location being called into question.
The holiday season was a cheerful one for retailers, and Wedbush analyst Christopher Svezia expects Under Armour UAA, -0.28% to exceed “low” expectations in the quarterly results. 
Still, consumers’ perception of the Under Armour brand could be slipping.
The FactSet consensus is for break-even results on a per share basis with sales of $1.32 billion, compared with 23 cents per share and $1.31 billion in sales for the same period last year.
Read: Bill Ackman’s Pershing Square reveals stake in Nike 
“It is clear that consumer interest [in] the Under Armour brand is not what it once was, as seen in its North American sales declines and its recent first sales decline in memory,” Wedbush said in a note published Wednesday. Among the problems are “undifferentiated product,” a failure to focus on key products and categories, and its strong ties to sports, which precludes its ability to build a fashion brand.
The company’s sportswear collection “has not been relevant,” according to Svezia.
Svezia also points to competition from brands including Asics, Champion and Reebok; the need for marketing to be more closely aligned to consumer lifestyles; and debt covenants that may need amending during fiscal 2018.
“What has damaged the brand is distribution into too many accounts overall and perhaps poor product segmentation, coupled with [misforecasting] demand, creating inventory issues and driving promotions,” the note says, highlighting expansion into Kohl’s Corp. KSS, -1.96% , DSW Inc. DSW, -0.94% and Famous Footwear. All of those wholesalers also sell Nike Inc. NKE, +1.46% , Adidas AG ADS, +1.22% , Puma and Reebok, and the expansion isn’t frowned upon, though the company may need to pull back from lower-margin accounts.
Read: Kohl’s upgraded as investments show signs of long-term growth potential 
Svezia wonders aloud whether Under Armour’s new Fifth Avenue flagship store in New York is a good idea, citing data from Cushman & Wakefield that puts rent at $3,000 per square foot per year, among the most expensive in the world. The space will be located near an Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.19% location, and take up 53,000 square feet.
“While intrigued, we feel this is not the right move, particularly given the rent may come at an estimated $159 million per year,” he said.
Wedbush rates Under Armour shares neutral with a $12 price target.
Susquehanna Financial Group analysts led by Sam Poser say that as the competition continues to gain momentum, Under Armour could feel an intensifying pinch. Moreover, after visiting the Outdoor Retailer show last week, analysts wonder if it’s not just shoppers that could be turning away from Under Armour. 
The Under Armour booth was “generally very quiet,” and feedback from other brands, according to the Susquehanna analysts, was negative. “One manager of a large national brand told us that he was receiving, for the first time, a multitude of job applications from current Under Armour employees,” analysts said.

Susquehanna rates Under Armour shares sell with an $11 price target.
Overall, according to Susquehanna, the Outdoor Retailer show demonstrated that cold weather was helping the sector reach “some of the best results in about four years.” Analysts think VF Corp. VFC, -1.00% , whose portfolio of brands includes the North Face and Timberland, Skechers Inc. SKX, +2.39% , and Dick’s Sporting Goods Inc. DKS, -3.38% are “positioned best.” 
Under Armour shares are up 13% over the last three months, but they’re down 34.2% in the past year. The S&P 500 index SPX, -0.15% is up 9.8% in the past three months, and the SPDR S&P Retail ETF XRT, -1.16% is up more than 20% for the period.
